units.source_text: 古歌：“此身化灰烬，没入白云里。

en.t: An old poem says, "This body turns to ashes and vanishes into the white clouds.

units.source_text: 君欲觅我时，但见荒烟起。”

en.t: When you wish to seek me, you will see only desolate smoke rising."

units.source_text: 又：“此身投沧海，没入荒波里。

en.t: And another says, "This body casts itself into the blue sea and sinks among the wild waves.

units.source_text: 消失同水泡，谁复思念你？”

en.t: It disappears like foam on the water; who will ever think of you again?"
This appears in the Shinchokusen Collection.

units.source_text: 此处所引用“没入”二字，出自此二古歌。

en.t: The two characters quoted here as "sinking into" come from these two old poems.

units.source_text: 前者与复诗中“化雨云”相关联；

en.t: The former is connected with the phrase "turning into rain clouds" in the reply poem;

units.source_text: 后者与浮舟后来投水相关联。

en.t: the latter is connected with Ukifune later throwing herself into the water.
